title: Pipe Insulation System
model_title: Pipe Insulation System (Hot Service, Layered Cutaway)

introduction.definition: A pipe insulation system reduces heat loss from hot lines (or heat gain to cold lines), keeps process temperatures stable, protects people from hot surfaces and prevents condensation. A hot-service system typically has an anti-corrosion coating, one or more insulation layers with staggered joints, and a weatherproof metal cladding with bands, plus insulated supports.
applications: Hot process lines (alumina digestion liquor, oil)
key_points: Wet insulation loses most of its insulating value
Corrosion under insulation (CUI) is a major hazard

classification.type: Hot-service insulation (mineral wool / calcium silicate) with metal cladding

introduction.summary: A pipe insulation system reduces heat loss (or gain) from piping, keeps process temperatures stable, protects personnel from hot surfaces and prevents condensation on cold lines. A typical hot-service system has an anti-corrosion coating on the pipe, one or more insulation layers with staggered joints, and a weatherproof metal cladding held by bands, plus insulated supports.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Heat loss falls steeply with the first centimetres of insulation, then more slowly (economic thickness).

heat_loss.title: Heat loss
heat_loss.description: Bare pipe (left) loses heat strongly by convection and radiation; under the insulation (right) the heat flow is a fraction of that. Heat loss per metre ≈ 2πk(T_pipe − T_surface)/ln(r_out/r_in). Insulation also keeps the surface below touch-safe temperature (personnel protection, typically ≤ 60 °C — verify local regulations).

foundation: Support pipework at the intervals and on the support types shown on the piping drawings; allow for thermal expansion.
alignment: Fit up joints within code tolerances; do not force flanges.
piping: Coat and dry the pipe before insulating.
Stagger joints between layers; overlap cladding to shed water; seal penetrations.
commissioning: Flush/blow the line, then hydrotest or pneumatic test to code.
Reinstate instruments and remove test blinds.

video_tutorials.title: Pipe Insulation System — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Pipe Insulation System.
A pipe insulation system reduces heat loss from hot lines (or heat gain to cold lines), keeps process temperatures stable, protects people from hot surfaces and prevents condensation.
A hot-service system typically has an anti-corrosion coating, one or more insulation layers with staggered joints, and a weatherproof metal cladding with bands, plus insulated supports.
Typical applications include steam and condensate lines; hot process lines (alumina digestion liquor, oil); cold/cryogenic lines (with vapour barrier); personnel protection.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Pipe Insulation System — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Pipe Insulation System.
Inspect cladding for damage and open seams.
Thermographic survey for hot spots.
Remove insulation at suspect locations for CUI inspection.
Watch for corrosion under insulation (cui): hidden wall loss, leaks. Common cause: water ingress through damaged cladding.
Watch for wet / damaged insulation: hot spots, energy loss. Common cause: mechanical damage, rain.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
